title: Mira Ceti, Atypical Archetype
question: Unravel the complexity of the morpho-kinematics and nascent wind generation mechanisms of the circumstellar envelope (CSE) of Mira Ceti.

recipe.goal: Analyze SiO(5-4) line width and test for inner CSE rotation (5 to 15 au)
recipe.method: Extract Doppler velocity spectra averaged in 30 mas broad annular rings centered on Mira A (from 25 to 215 mas in 10 mas steps) with a 3-sigma cut; measure full-width at 1/5 maximum; test velocity gradient impact by re-centering spectra in 30x30 mas^2 pixels; fit sine waves to mean Doppler velocity <V_z> vs position angle omega in ring 30<R<100 mas.
key_parameters: 3-sigma cut; 30 mas annular rings from 25 to 215 mas in 10 mas steps; 30 < R < 100 mas ring; V_z intervals of +-10 and +-17 km s^-1
assumptions: Distance of 100 pc (10 mas = 1 au); systemic velocity V_LSR = 47.7 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Map and compare 13CO(3-2), 12CO(3-2), and SiO(5-4) morpho-kinematics in the central region (region C)
recipe.method: Select region C where |V_z| < 4 km s^-1 and 12CO(3-2) intensity exceeds 10 Jy arcsec^-2 km s^-1; extrapolate radial intensity in 1<R<2 arcsec to R=0 to measure central concentration; rotate coordinates (x,y) clockwise by 35 deg to (x',y'); construct integrated PV maps along x' and y' and measure integrated fluxes and ratios for 5 kinematic fragments (NEA, SWO, NEO, SWS, SEO).
key_parameters: |V_z| < 4 km s^-1; 12CO intensity > 10 Jy arcsec^-2 km s^-1; coordinate rotation angle 35 deg; fragment boundaries in x', y', V_z from Table 3
assumptions: Unresolved central continuum contribution of ~2.7 Jy km s^-1 excluded from central radial extrapolation

recipe.goal: Derive mass loss rates for the SEO and NEO fragments from 13CO(3-2) flux
recipe.method: Calculate mass per unit radius M_R from optically thin 13CO(3-2) flux per unit radius F_R using level population and molecular constants, then multiply by projected radial wind velocity V_R: M_dot = M_R * V_R.
key_parameters: A_ji = 2.18e-6 s^-1, E_u = 31.7 K for 13CO(3-2); V_R(SEO) = 3.0+-0.5 km s^-1; V_R(NEO) = 2.9+-0.8 km s^-1; radial extension 1.0+-0.2 arcsec (SEO) and 1.5+-0.3 arcsec (NEO)
assumptions: Optically thin 13CO(3-2) emission; temperature profile T[K] = 109 / r[arcsec] (~50 to 200 K); 12C/13C isotopic ratio = 12; 12CO/H2 abundance = 4e-4; distance = 100 pc

recipe.goal: Determine SiO/CO abundance ratio outside the south-western quadrant and compare with RS Cnc and EP Aqr
recipe.method: Measure SiO(5-4) to 13CO(3-2) intensity ratios in fragments outside the south-western quadrant; convert emissivity ratio to column density and abundance ratio in the optically thin limit; compare radial profiles of SiO(5-4) and CO(3-2) (scaling CO(2-1) to CO(3-2) for RS Cnc and EP Aqr) beyond 100 au.
key_parameters: Excluded south-western quadrant: 200 deg < omega < 315 deg; A_21 = 6.91e-7 s^-1, A_32 = 2.50e-6 s^-1, E_u21 = 16.6 K, E_u32 = 33.2 K, A_SiO(5-4) = 5.2e-4 s^-1, E_u,SiO = 31.3 K
SiO/13CO column density to emissivity ratio factor ~7.5e-3; SiO(5-4)/13CO(3-2) intensity ratio ~0.1
assumptions: Optically thin approximation for SiO(5-4) and 13CO(3-2) outside the central region; 12CO/13CO abundance ratio = 12; temperature law T[K] = 109 / r[arcsec]

score_reason: Archival ALMA project codes are explicitly stated and public, and the coordinate transformations, kinematic cuts (Table 3), and analytical formulas for mass loss rate and abundance ratios are clearly given in the text. However, calibration and imaging details are delegated to an earlier paper (HTN20) and custom analysis scripts are not released.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA datasets (2011.0.00014.SV and 2013.1.00047.S) with explicit kinematic bounding boxes in Table 3 and closed-form equations for mass-loss rates, line widths, and sine-wave rotation fits.
